# DropSpace 1.1 Beta2

## Changes

- The independent music window consumes the same word timing as the Island. Timed lyrics fill within each word, including CJK text and wrapped rows. Tracks without word timings retain line highlighting.
- The flowing background responds to the existing fresh process-loopback signal. No separate audio capture or media observer is created.
- Inactive lyrics gradually blur after inactivity. Nearby lines remain more readable, farther lines blur more, and text fades at the upper and lower viewport edges. Scrolling or navigating lyrics restores readability; transport, volume, translation and window adjustments preserve the focus effect.
- Music controls use balanced responsive layouts. Portrait and split lyric layouts match their bottom and side insets; the landscape cover view remains centered. Lyrics and translation controls stay below system volume.
- All four regular Island pages keep the same size. The music page adapts artwork and spacing to the actual lyric font and available interior, including the largest supported lyric size.
- AI lyric glow reuses its drawing buffers through Island expansion and collapse instead of repeatedly allocating large arrays. The light keeps the same pixels and eligibility rules while avoiding the measured garbage-collection stalls.
- Island retrieval starts without an implicit selection. Repeated clicks, the clear-selection action and Escape can deselect results. Image previews temporarily enlarge the Island, and Back restores the results layout.
- Music presentation is disposed on its owning UI dispatcher during shutdown, fixing the logged shutdown exception.

v1.1.0-beta.1 is the immediate upgrade baseline for this release. Existing content, settings, providers, model files and independent CUDA component bytes are preserved.

## Downloads and requirements

Windows x64 build 20348 or later. Choose `DropSpaceSetup.exe`, the portable `DropSpace.exe`, or the MSIX package. Stable remains 1.0. Portable updates use manual replacement.

## Validation and known limits

Focused native checks and Computer Use inspected word fill, lyric focus, responsive presentation, selection and enlarged previews. Real Apple Music playback confirmed shared word timing and process-loopback-driven background response. Synthetic timed fixtures separately cover partial English/CJK words. See the [validation record](../../docs/dev/1.1-beta2-local-delivery.md) for the complete executed checks and remaining coverage limits.

The reported 2026-10-26 background native heap crash (`0xc0000374`) has not been reproduced or proven fixed. There is no accessible matching dump. The shutdown fix is a separate demonstrated defect and is not presented as a cure for that incident. A short successful playback run does not establish long-term stability.
